agent_impl: examples/supplier_agent.py: a LangGraph StateGraph, six steps in a chain, unchanged but for the synapse0g import and compile
dataset: synthetic supplier marketplace (synapse0g/agents/supplier_desk.py), 60 requests; right answers computed by code from the purchasing policy

findings.message: langgraph:load_policy has only literal arguments, but it is a tool node with effect pure; evaluating it at compile time could do something observable.

estimate.note: no pure deterministic transform here has all-literal arguments
every node contributes to an output or to an effect
every model call in this graph reads all of its arguments
no two nodes in this graph compute the same thing
this graph has no loop region

transformations.description: load_policy (langgraph:load_policy) is pure and may now be served from the cache, keyed on every argument
n_state (langgraph_state) is pure and may now be served from the cache, keyed on every argument

findings.message: langgraph:get_quotes is an unseeded stochastic call; collapsing two samples into one would change the output distribution even though neither call touched the world.
langgraph:screen_reviews is an unseeded stochastic call; collapsing two samples into one would change the output distribution even though neither call touched the world.
langgraph:check_certificates is an unseeded stochastic call; collapsing two samples into one would change the output distribution even though neither call touched the world.
langgraph:decide is an unseeded stochastic call; collapsing two samples into one would change the output distribution even though neither call touched the world.
langgraph:place_order is irreversible (it moves money or destroys data); it is never cached, re-ordered or re-run.

estimate.note: 2 node(s) are cacheable, but this graph has never run, so there is no measured hit rate to predict from

transformations.description: load_policy, get_quotes, screen_reviews, check_certificates have no data or effect edge between them and now run concurrently (limit 4)

findings.message: langgraph:place_order has an observable side effect; its position relative to other side-effecting nodes is fixed and never reordered.

estimate.note: up to 4 concurrent (limit 8); 1 independent group(s), 0 map region(s)
no model call here can move to a cheaper model

compile.explain:
supplier_check: 6 steps, as written: load_policy -> get_quotes -> screen_reviews -> check_certificates -> decide -> place_order
  load_policy          pure          reads -; waits for nothing
  get_quotes           read          reads rfq; waits for nothing
  screen_reviews       read          reads rfq; waits for nothing
  check_certificates   read          reads rfq; waits for nothing
  decide               pure          reads certificates, checklist, quotes, review_flags, rfq; waits for check_certificates, get_quotes, load_policy, screen_reviews
  place_order          irreversible  reads certificates, checklist, order, quotes, receipt, review_flags, rfq; waits for check_certificates, decide, get_quotes, load_policy, screen_reviews
  applied  memoize: load_policy (langgraph:load_policy) is pure and may now be served from the cache, keyed on every argument
  applied  memoize: n_state (langgraph_state) is pure and may now be served from the cache, keyed on every argument
  applied  parallelize: load_policy, get_quotes, screen_reviews, check_certificates have no data or effect edge between them and now run concurrently (limit 4)
  refused  memoize on place_order: langgraph:place_order is irreversible (it moves money or destroys data); it is never cached, re-ordered or re-run.
  refused  parallelize on place_order: langgraph:place_order has an observable side effect; its position relative to other side-effecting nodes is fixed and never reordered.
